prompt: Which random variable has a binomial distribution?

choices.label: The number of rolls of a fair die until the first 6 appears.
The number of 6s in 10 rolls of a fair die.
The number of hearts in 5 cards dealt without replacement from one deck.
The height, in cm, of a randomly chosen student.

hint: Binomial needs BINS: Binary outcomes, Independent trials, a fixed Number of trials, and the Same probability each trial.

hints.text: Binomial needs BINS: Binary outcomes, Independent trials, a fixed Number of trials, and the Same probability each trial.
Counting trials until the first success is geometric, not binomial. Dealing without replacement breaks independence. A height is not a count at all.
Only B has a fixed number of trials ($n = 10$), each independent with the same $p = \frac{1}{6}$, and counts successes.

explanation: A binomial variable counts successes in a FIXED number of independent trials with the same success probability.
A has no fixed $n$ (you roll until a 6) — that is geometric. C changes the probability after each card, so trials are not independent. D is a measurement, not a count.
B: 10 trials, each a 6 or not, independent, $p = \frac{1}{6}$ every time. That is binomial.

alternativeExplanations.title: Ask "what am I counting?"
steps: Binomial counts HOW MANY successes in $n$ tries. Geometric counts HOW LONG until the first success.
B counts how many 6s in 10 tries — binomial. A counts how long until a 6 — geometric.
C and D fail for other reasons (no independence; not a count).
